releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.8
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.8 — Gemini quota is back in `accounts quota`

Runs, account selection and cooldowns behave as in 0.9.7. This release fixes `accounts quota --refresh`, which had stopped reporting the Gemini pool.

## Changes since 0.9.7

**Gemini quota snapshots.** Cloud Code now returns the Gemini group from `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` only when the request's User-Agent names a recent agy CLI (`antigravity/cli/<version> (...)`, as agy itself sends). agy-crew sent a bare `antigravity`, so every refresh came back with the Claude/GPT pool only: `accounts list` and `accounts quota` showed no `gemini` rows, and `auto` could neither rank accounts by Gemini quota left nor skip an account whose Gemini quota was empty. agy's own usage view was unaffected.

Quota requests now send `antigravity/cli/<version> (aidev_client; os_type=<os>; arch=<arch>)`, with the version read from `agy --version` once per refresh (1.4.9 when it cannot be read). Run `agy-crew accounts quota --refresh` once after upgrading to bring the Gemini snapshots back.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
agy-crew accounts quota --refresh
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.7
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.7 — login with an id_token_email token

Runs, account selection and quota handling behave as in 0.9.6. This release fixes account login with token files written by newer agy versions.

## Changes since 0.9.6

**Login no longer fails on an `id_token_email` token.** agy records the signed-in account in its token file either as an `id_token` JWT or, in newer versions, as a plain `id_token_email` field. agy-crew only read the JWT, so a sign-in that produced the second form failed with `could not read an email from the token; refusing to add an account that cannot be told apart`, and a re-login of such an account was rolled back. The email is now read from either field. Accounts already in the pool need nothing.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.6
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.6 — interactive start, help and refresh progress

Runs, account selection and quota handling behave as in 0.9.5. This release adds a way to use a pool account by hand, a readable help text, a `version` command, and progress output for `accounts quota --refresh`.

## Changes since 0.9.5

**`start`.** `agy-crew start <name> [-- <agy args>...]` runs agy interactively in the current terminal and directory as pool account `<name>`, with that account's private HOME, so there is no separate agy login to manage. Arguments after `--` reach agy unchanged, and the command exits with agy's exit code. While agy runs the account is held as by `accounts hold acquire`: `auto` never picks it, it never lends, and its token is never swapped by a loan. The hold ends when agy exits. `start` is refused before launch for an unknown, disabled, signed-out or busy account; a cooldown is only noted on stderr. Without a name it lists the accounts with their state and an example. See [Interactive sessions](../REFERENCE.md#interactive-sessions).

**Help and version.** `agy-crew` with no arguments now prints a grouped overview of every command instead of a one-paragraph usage error; `help` (`--help`, `-h`) prints the same on stdout and exits 0. `version` (`--version`, `-v`) prints the versions of agy-crew and agy.

**Quota refresh progress.** `accounts quota --refresh` used to print nothing until every account was done, and renewing an expired token through agy takes several seconds per account. It now reports on stderr: one `✓`/`✗` line with the time taken per account and, on a terminal, a live line with the account, what it is waiting on and for how long. stdout still carries only the table or JSON, and `--json` off a terminal prints no progress. Accounts are still refreshed one at a time.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.5
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.5 — external holds

Runs, account selection and quota handling behave as in 0.9.4. This release adds a way for another program that uses a pool account's credential to keep agy-crew off that account while it does, and to report quota resets it learns.

## Changes since 0.9.4

**`accounts hold`.** `accounts hold acquire <name> --pid <pid> [--family <f>] [--json]` holds an account for the process `<pid>`; `accounts hold release <id>` ends the hold, and it also ends when that process exits. While an account is held:

- `auto` never picks it and it never lends its credential;
- an explicit `--account <name>` for it fails before launch;
- a conversation bound to it continues on a borrowed credential, as when its account is cooling;
- `list` shows it as `held`, and `remove` and `login` refuse it.

A hold is refused when agy-crew has no such account (`unknown`), when the account has another lease or loan (`busy`), or, with `--family`, when that family is cooling or its quota snapshot is empty (with `retry_at`). With `--json` a refusal prints `{ "refused": ... }` and exits 1. See [External holds](../REFERENCE.md#external-holds).

**`accounts cooldown record`.** `accounts cooldown record <name> --family <f> --retry-at <time>` records a quota cooldown learned outside agy-crew. It never shortens a cooldown already in force.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.

releases.name: agy-crew v0.9.4
releases.body:
# agy-crew 0.9.4 — account rotation on upstream 503

The account pool, quota handling and the other commands behave as in 0.9.3. This release fixes what happens when the model has no capacity, and makes `auto` rotate between accounts.

## Changes since 0.9.3

**An upstream 503 now rotates accounts.** `UNAVAILABLE (code 503): No capacity available for model ...` matched no failure class, so the run ended at once with no cooldown and no failover, and the next run picked the same account again. It is now its own reason, `upstream_unavailable`:

- The account is parked for that model family for 3 minutes, so the next selection, in the same run or a separate one, uses another account. The short cooldown never shortens a quota cooldown that is still running.
- A new task that changed nothing (`ask` always; other modes when `git status` shows nothing new) is rerun from its original prompt as a new conversation on another account. It is a rewrite, not a continuation. If the workspace was already changed, the run continues the conversation on a borrowed credential, as for quota. An explicit `--account` is never moved. At most two extra attempts are made, because agy already retries a 503 for about two minutes itself.
- When every account is cooling only because of 503s the error says `upstream_unavailable`, not `quota_exhausted`. A background job stops in `attention` (or `error` without a conversation) with `retry_at`.

**`auto` rotates between similar accounts.** Ranking compared remaining quota exactly, so the fullest account won every time even right after it was used. Known quota is now compared in 5% steps, and accounts within a step rotate by least recent use. An account that is clearly fuller still wins.

**Skills.** The jobs skill and its troubleshooting reference tell the orchestrator: on `upstream_unavailable`, if agy had not done anything yet, rewrite the task and start a new run (`restart <job id>` or a fresh dispatch), and do not use `continue`, because a continuation stays bound to the same account and conversation and has nothing to continue from. Use `continue` only after agy changed the workspace, and only after inspecting it.

## Upgrading

```bash
npm install -g agy-crew@latest
agy-crew install
```

Restart the harness. No migration is needed.
